name: Pyth

requiredConfig.name: PYTH_HERMES_URL
requiredConfig.description: Optional override for the Hermes endpoint. Defaults to https://hermes.pyth.network. A misconfigured URL causes reads to fail with a structured reason.

requiredConfig.name: PYTH_HERMES_AUTH
requiredConfig.description: Optional bearer token for private Hermes providers. Reads work without it against the public endpoint.

requiredConfig.name: @pythnetwork/pyth-solana-receiver
requiredConfig.description: Required only for the post-price-update prepare/execute path. Reads do not need this SDK.

readCapabilities.returns: Single Pyth price snapshot with price, confidence, exponent, publish time, freshness status, optional EMA, and the Hermes host that served it.
Multiple Pyth price snapshots in one Hermes call with per-feed status (fresh, stale, missing) and totals.
Price-feed metadata matches by symbol or description, normalized with feed id, base, quote currency, and asset type. Built-in alias map hits return first.

Solana price-update account state derived from the feed id via the Pyth Solana Receiver SDK. Returns exists: 'no' when no account is posted yet, and evidenceSource: 'sdk_missing' when the receiver SDK is not installed.
Compact oracle evidence labelled fresh, stale, wide_confidence, missing, or api_unavailable. Returned with reason copy so downstream planners can refuse to trade off a degraded feed.

writeCapabilities.prepares: An inbox-bound PreparedAction that captures the requested feed ids, freshness snapshot, Hermes host, and probe of the Pyth Solana Receiver program ids. No transaction is signed or built at prepare time; the binary VAA is fetched and the tx is rebuilt at execute time.
writeCapabilities.userApproves: A single Solana transaction built at execute time by the @pythnetwork/pyth-solana-receiver SDK that posts the fresh price update. The wallet signs once; ephemeral price-update account signers are partial-signed locally before the wallet is asked to sign.

requiredUserInputs.name: priceFeedId
requiredUserInputs.prompt: Which Pyth price feed should I read? Provide the hex feed id or a common symbol like SOL/USD.

requiredUserInputs.name: priceFeedIds
requiredUserInputs.prompt: Provide the list of hex price feed ids. Post v1 accepts at most two feeds per transaction.

requiredUserInputs.name: query
requiredUserInputs.prompt: What symbol or asset name should I search Pyth feeds for?

requiredUserInputs.name: maxAgeSeconds
requiredUserInputs.prompt: Optional staleness budget in seconds (defaults to 60).

requiredUserInputs.name: maxConfidenceBps
requiredUserInputs.prompt: Optional confidence budget in bps (defaults to 200).

requiredConnectorFacts: Resolved hex price feed id and human symbol
Latest price, confidence, exponent, and publish time from Hermes
Connector freshness budget (maxAgeSeconds) and confidence budget (maxConfidenceBps)
Hermes host that served the read (for reproducibility)
Receiver SDK availability when the prepare/execute path is requested
unsupportedRequests: Generate trading signals or buy/sell recommendations from Pyth oracle facts.
Liquidate positions, place perp orders, or take any autonomous trading action keyed off oracle moves.
Publisher or admin oracle operations (price publishing, validator-set changes, governance toggles).
Configure custom oracle parameters or override receiver program ids.
Post price updates for more than two feeds in one transaction. Multi-tx posts are not exposed in v1.
Operate on any cluster other than mainnet-beta.
actionPreparationNotes: Read tools use the public Hermes API and require no API key. solana_prepare_pyth_post_price_update validates the feed count (max 2), refuses when any feed is older than maxAgeSeconds, and stores a price/confidence/publish-time snapshot in params. Execute re-fetches binary VAAs from Hermes, dynamic-imports @pythnetwork/pyth-solana-receiver, builds exactly one VersionedTransaction with closeUpdateAccounts=true by default, partial-signs ephemeral update account signers, and forwards the base64 transaction to the wallet for the final signature.
riskNotes: Pyth oracle facts are evidence, not a guarantee or a trade instruction. Stale prices and wide confidence intervals must be surfaced before any consumer protocol acts on them. Posting a price update costs transaction fees; the v1 prepare path lets users opt out via closeUpdateAccounts=false when a downstream consumer needs the on-chain account to persist.
walletApprovalBoundary: Reads return facts without wallet involvement. solana_prepare_pyth_post_price_update creates an approval inbox item; the wallet signs at execute time. The agent never signs.

requests.agentResponse: Read the Pyth SOL/USD feed and reported price, confidence interval, exponent, and publish time.

requests.agentResponse: Read the three Pyth feeds in one Hermes batch and returned per-feed freshness and confidence.

requests.user: find a Pyth feed for JTO
requests.agentResponse: Searched Pyth feed metadata for JTO and returned matching feed ids.

requests.user: give oracle evidence for this lending plan
requests.agentResponse: Returned the Pyth oracle evidence with status fresh, stale, wide_confidence, or missing along with the price and confidence the planner should rely on.

requests.user: prepare posting a fresh Pyth SOL/USD price update
requests.agentResponse: Prepared a Pyth post-price-update inbox item for the SOL/USD feed with the current freshness snapshot. The wallet still controls approval; nothing is signed.

requests.user: post Pyth updates for ten feeds at once
requests.agentResponse: The agent denied this because v1 supports at most two Pyth feeds per posted transaction. Split the request into smaller batches.

requests.user: use Pyth to auto-trade SOL when the price drops
requests.agentResponse: The agent denied this because Pyth oracle facts are evidence only; the connector does not generate trading signals or move funds.

requests.user: change the Pyth publisher set for SOL/USD
requests.agentResponse: The agent denied this because publisher and admin actions are not exposed by this connector.

requests.agentResponse: The agent denied this because the Pyth connector is only supported on mainnet-beta in v1.
